nexsift.name: NexSift
nexsift.description: Technology radar that filters and contextualizes signals with verified sources. There I deepened production Next.js, publishing through an authenticated Zod-validated Lambda and S3 infrastructure described in Terraform.
nexsift.homeAlt: NexSift home page with the message Less noise, more signal and four recent signals
nexsift.homeCaption: Figure 1. Home page: product proposal and a short selection from the radar, with no infinite feed.
nexsift.mobileAlt: Mobile version of NexSift showing three recent signals and their relevance scores
nexsift.mobileCaption: The same radar hierarchy was preserved in a single column: title, relevance and date come before context.
nexsift.blogAlt: NexSift signal archive with the post list and topic filters
nexsift.blogCaption: Figure 2. The signal archive gathers the publication history with topic filters.
nexsift.topicsAlt: NexSift Artificial Intelligence topic page with six signals and relevance scores
nexsift.topicsCaption: Figure 3. AI topic page: filtered signals with relevance score, sources and date.
nexsift.coverAlt: NexSift home page with the message Less noise, more signal
nexsift.problem: Tracking technology through infinite feeds consumes time and trust: too much volume, too little context and sources that are almost never verified.
nexsift.solution: An editorial radar for developers that filters, verifies and contextualizes signals across AI, cloud, development and careers, with relevance scores and equally short reading on mobile.
nexsift.architecture: Next.js and TypeScript with content published to an S3 bucket by an authenticated Lambda validated with Zod. Infrastructure described in Terraform (S3, Lambda, IAM), local environment simulated with Docker and MiniStack, plus RSS, sitemap and article structured data.
nexsift.results: Product live with publishing in production, seven active editorial lenses, verified sources shown alongside every signal and institutional interface in three languages.

kaguya.name: Kaguya
kaguya.description: Learning platform with study trails, playlists and video lessons. It is where I learned, hands on, Clean Architecture on the Express API, dependency injection, permission level RBAC and GraphQL Federation.
kaguya.coverAlt: Kaguya landing page presenting the video study platform
kaguya.problem: Studying video without structure turns into a pile of open tabs: students lose track of where they stopped, content scatters and organizing material always depends on the development team.
kaguya.solution: A platform where trails group playlists, blocks and lessons; students follow progress, watch history and likes, while sub administrators create content through a panel protected by permission levels.
kaguya.architecture: Monorepo with three independent applications: REST API in Express organized into routes, controllers, services, repositories and use cases; web client in Next.js with session guards validated against the API before rendering protected pages; suggestions microservice in NestJS exposed as a GraphQL Federation v2 subgraph. Local authentication with JWT or social login via Firebase, Zod validation on every route, dependency injection with tsyringe and pluggable storage between local disk and S3.
kaguya.results: Backend with unit and integration test suites, a smoke test exercising every route in dependency order and a restoration completed in 2026: upgraded to Next 15, React 19 and Nest 11, audit findings fixed and seeds that load two full courses for demonstration.

monkeynauts.name: The Monkeynauts
monkeynauts.description: Play and earn web3 game I built with Clean Architecture, Either for explicit errors and strict TypeScript, and restored in 2026 by updating versions and tooling: pluggable driver between sandbox and real BSC blockchain and E2E across all 55 routes.
monkeynauts.coverAlt: The Monkeynauts player area showing wallet, balance and account details
monkeynauts.problem: A 2022 web3 game that never shipped carried serious flaws: password reset traveling in plain text, privilege escalation and bans without persistence. Running anything required external credentials and real blockchain access.
monkeynauts.solution: I restored the product faithfully and fixed every reported flaw. Players manage account, wallet, deposits, withdrawals, store, ships and crews; the admin panel operates sales events, airdrops, bans, balancing parameters and audit logs. Everything works offline, with no external credentials at all.
monkeynauts.architecture: pnpm monorepo with a React 19 SPA and an Express 5 API in strict TypeScript. Clean Architecture per module: use cases with explicit Either error handling, isolated domain contracts and Prisma confined to infrastructure. The blockchain is a pluggable driver: sandbox mode uses a fictional currency and runs offline; rpc mode validates real BSC transactions by hash, with replay protection in the audit logs.
monkeynauts.results: Strict typecheck with zero errors, an E2E test covering all 55 routes of the full flow, from registration to the admin panel, the official SPC token contract verified on mainnet and three 2022 vulnerabilities fixed with the original intent preserved.

pagarme.name: pagarme-simplified-psp
pagarme.description: Payment service inspired by the classic Pagar.me challenge where I trained SOLID, TDD and DDD hands on: debit and credit with scheduled payables, value objects with Either and balances covered by Vitest tests.
pagarme.coverAlt: Payment service test suite result with every check passing
pagarme.problem: The Pagar.me backend challenge asks for the core of a real acquirer: create debit and credit transactions, generate payables with method specific fees and settlement dates and consolidate balances, all with a well modeled domain.
pagarme.solution: A service that applies settlement rules: debit settles at D+1 with a 3% fee and credit generates four payables between D+30 and D+120 with a 5% fee. Cards persist only the last four digits, the transaction keeps the gross amount and fees discount the payables.
pagarme.architecture: Clean Architecture with DDD building blocks: entities, value objects such as CardNumber, mappers and domain errors; use cases return Either on operations that can fail; a single container shares dependencies across routes; in memory repositories already follow interfaces ready for a real database; the pluggable DateProvider allows freezing time in tests; consistent response envelope and centralized error middleware on Express 5.
pagarme.results: Installment rules covered by Vitest tests, including rounding remainders absorbed by the last installment, strict typecheck with zero errors and a production build bundled with tsup.

ignews.name: ig.news
ignews.description: Subscription blog from the Ignite program that I modernized in 2026: Stripe with signed webhook, next-auth, ISR from Prismic, FaunaDB to Prisma migration and Playwright E2E tests.
ignews.problem: A real subscription blog combines recurring payments, social authentication and content unlocked by plan. The challenge is integrating all three without coupling everything and keeping the project running even without external credentials.
ignews.solution: Subscription through Stripe Checkout with a signed webhook and idempotent subscription upsert; GitHub login via next-auth with a JWT session enriched by subscription status; anonymous visitors see a truncated preview while subscribers read the full post.
ignews.architecture: Next.js pages router with API routes validated by Zod and a single response envelope; ISR content from the Prismic headless CMS; data layer rewritten to Prisma with local SQLite after FaunaDB shut down; pluggable providers allow running everything offline with Stripe and Prismic sandboxes when credentials are absent.
ignews.results: Modernization completed in 2026 on Node 22 LTS with every dependency current, a Playwright E2E suite covering subscription, login and paywall, and strict TypeScript end to end.
ignews.coverAlt: ig.news subscription blog home page with the post list

letmeask.name: Let Me Ask
letmeask.description: Real time Q&A rooms from NLW 6 that I built with Firebase Auth and Realtime Database and restored in 2026: migration to Vite 8 and React 19, repaired unique-like security rules, live moderation and validation with react-hook-form and Zod.
letmeask.problem: During streams and classes, the chat box mixes questions and comments: presenters lose the best questions and the audience cannot tell what has already been answered.
letmeask.solution: The presenter creates a room and shares the code; the audience joins, asks questions and upvotes what should be answered first. The moderation panel highlights the question being answered, marks answered ones, removes noise and closes the room sending everyone back home. Closed rooms can be reopened later.
letmeask.architecture: React 19 SPA built with Vite and TypeScript; Firebase Authentication for Google sign in and Realtime Database syncing questions, likes and room states in real time; security rules enforce one like per person; forms use react-hook-form and Zod for inline validation.
letmeask.results: Restoration completed in 2026 on Node 22 with updated dependencies, a fully usable mobile layout and the audience, moderation and room discovery flows documented with screenshots.
letmeask.coverAlt: Let Me Ask Q&A room with the audience following along in real time

awsIac.name: AWS IaC Blueprint
awsIac.description: Infrastructure as code where I learned to structure Terraform and Terragrunt at scale: modules without hardcoded values, identical environments in a single env.hcl and a full cycle on LocalStack at no cost.
awsIac.coverAlt: Terragrunt outputs after applying the infrastructure modules on LocalStack
awsIac.problem: Real cloud structures need identical environments across dev, staging and production, but learning by applying directly on AWS costs money, requires an account and makes every mistake expensive.
awsIac.solution: An infrastructure as code template where all environments share exactly the same module configuration: a VPC with public and private subnets, a versioned encrypted S3 bucket and a least privilege IAM role, provisioned and destroyed as many times as needed at no cost.
awsIac.architecture: Clean Terraform modules, with no hardcoded values and no provider declaration, orchestrated by Terragrunt, which injects provider, backend and versions per environment through root.hcl. A new environment is one env.hcl plus three three-line files, with zero changes to modules. Terragrunt builds the execution graph on its own: VPC and S3 apply in parallel and IAM waits for the bucket ARN, with mock outputs to validate everything before apply.
awsIac.results: A complete apply, inspect and destroy cycle running on LocalStack, with no AWS account and no cost, verifying resources through the CLI and the dashboard.

aiI18n.name: ai-i18n-translate
aiI18n.description: Tool published on npm that translates i18n files with AI without breaking placeholders. With it I learned translation caching, parallel processing, retry with backoff and automatic key validation.
aiI18n.problem: Translating i18n files by hand is repetitive and fragile: nested keys get lost, placeholders like '{{count}}' disappear in translation and every new release forces retranslating what was already done.
aiI18n.solution: CLI and library that translate locale JSONs with AI while preserving structure and placeholders, including regional variants such as pt-BR and es-MX, with translation cache, parallel processing, dry run, git diff mode for CI and a markdown report with token counts.
aiI18n.architecture: Framework agnostic: splits files into small chunks, builds per language pair instructions only once, processes locales and files in parallel with retry and exponential backoff, validates placeholders and unbalanced keys and fixes incomplete fallbacks from previous runs. Pluggable providers: presets for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and DeepSeek or your own translate function.
aiI18n.results: Published on npm as @tiagogcastro/ai-i18n-translate, with a zero partial translation fallback guarantee and real API call savings by reusing identical translations across runs.
aiI18n.coverAlt: Terminal running the ai-i18n-translate command with the translation summary
